vignette: Raj is a 36-year-old South Asian male detective married to his high school sweetheart, Priya. Growing up in a small town, Raj's childhood was marred by physical abuse from his father, who would often lose control and lash out at him for minor infractions or no reason at all. The abuse left deep emotional scars that have persisted into adulthood. In the present day, Raj finds himself struggling with flashbacks of those traumatic moments, especially when he is under stress on the job. As a detective, his work frequently exposes him to violent crime scenes and disturbing cases, which often trigger memories of his own past trauma. The other night, while working on an assault case that involved physical violence similar to what he experienced as a child, Raj found himself unable to focus. He could almost feel his father's heavy hand again, hear the sound of fists striking skin. At home, Raj tries to hide these feelings from Priya but often finds himself emotionally distant and irritable. Small things, like Priya’s nagging about cleaning up or making sure he eats on time, can set off a chain reaction of anger that surprises even him. He feels guilty afterward, knowing his reactions are disproportionate, but the fear and anxiety that follow such outbursts leave him feeling isolated. Raj has begun to notice how his sleep is affected by these recurring thoughts. Nightmares have become frequent, often leaving him awake in the middle of the night, drenched in sweat with a racing heart. He’ll lie awake, replaying scenes from both his childhood and recent cases at work, unable to distinguish between them. His job as a detective demands precision and focus, but Raj finds himself struggling to concentrate during meetings or while reviewing case files. His mind wanders back to the abuse, making it hard for him to stay present in the moment. Colleagues have noticed his occasional lapses, commenting that he seems distracted lately, which only adds to his feelings of inadequacy and guilt. In an attempt to manage these symptoms, Raj has taken up running as a way to cope with stress. The physical exertion helps him feel more grounded and gives him some semblance of control over his body. However, even this outlet sometimes brings back memories of being chased or physically overpowered by his father. Raj’s relationship with Priya has also been affected; he often feels the need to push her away when she tries to offer support. He fears that if he lets himself be vulnerable, he’ll break down completely. These moments of emotional withdrawal have left Priya feeling hurt and confused about their marriage. Despite his efforts to maintain a facade of strength, Raj knows deep down that something is not right. Recently, during a particularly intense case where he had to interrogate a suspect who was physically aggressive, Raj found himself trembling with fear and anger. The memories from childhood surged back, making it difficult for him to stay composed. Afterward, he isolated himself in his office, struggling to breathe until the panic subsided. Raj’s life has become a series of coping mechanisms designed to keep his trauma at bay, but they only offer temporary relief. He knows that something needs to change, but the idea of seeking help is daunting. The prospect of revisiting those painful memories and emotions fills him with dread, yet he feels increasingly trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance. Despite his best efforts to compartmentalize his past from his present life as a detective and husband, Raj finds that the trauma continues to shape who he is today. The fear, anger, and guilt that linger from childhood have made it challenging for him to fully engage with his work or his marriage without being haunted by memories of the abuse.
